scenes.tts: Is the map already in the dividing cells, or is it brought in by the axons that arrive?
scenes.visual: Title card: Two Answers, a Year Apart. The smooth sheet with a thalamus below it. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Is the map already in the dividing cells, or is it brought in by the axons that arrive?

scenes.tts: Two answers were proposed a year apart.
scenes.visual: Two name cards: Rakic, 1988; O'Leary, 1989.
scenes.narration: Two answers were proposed a year apart.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-eight, Pasko Rakic proposed the protomap.
scenes.caption: In 1988, Pasko Rakic proposed the protomap.
scenes.visual: On screen: protomap, Rakic, 1988. A cutaway of the embryonic cortical wall.
scenes.narration: In 1988, Pasko Rakic proposed the protomap.

scenes.tts: Cortical progenitors lie in the ventricular zone, the layer of the brain wall next to the fluid-filled ventricle.
scenes.visual: The bottom layer of the wall highlights, labelled ventricular zone, with the ventricle beneath.
scenes.narration: Cortical progenitors lie in the ventricular zone, the layer of the brain wall next to the fluid-filled ventricle.

scenes.tts: Newborn neurons climb outward along radial glia, long scaffold cells that span the wall.
scenes.visual: Long fibres stretch from the ventricle to the surface; small neurons climb up them.
scenes.narration: Newborn neurons climb outward along radial glia, long scaffold cells that span the wall.

scenes.tts: So neurons born from one patch stack up in a column above it.
scenes.visual: Three patches of progenitors in different tints, each sending up a column of same-tinted neurons.
scenes.narration: So neurons born from one patch stack up in a column above it.

scenes.tts: If the patches already differ by position, the outline of the areas is laid down where the cells are made.
scenes.visual: The tinted columns line up with the future areas on the dorsal map above.
scenes.narration: If the patches already differ by position, the outline of the areas is laid down where the cells are made.

scenes.tts: Think of a city zoned into districts before a single house is built.
scenes.visual: A city plan with coloured zones and empty lots.
scenes.narration: Think of a city zoned into districts before a single house is built.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-nine, Dennis O'Leary proposed the protocortex.
scenes.caption: In 1989, Dennis O'Leary proposed the protocortex.
scenes.visual: On screen: protocortex, O'Leary, 1989. A uniform grey wall.
scenes.narration: In 1989, Dennis O'Leary proposed the protocortex.

scenes.tts: Here the young sheet has broadly similar potential everywhere.
scenes.visual: Every progenitor patch in the same grey.
scenes.narration: Here the young sheet has broadly similar potential everywhere.

scenes.tts: Areas emerge mainly from the axons that arrive from the thalamus.
scenes.visual: Thalamic axon bundles arrive from below, each in its own colour.
scenes.narration: Areas emerge mainly from the axons that arrive from the thalamus.

scenes.tts: Different thalamic nuclei send axons to different parts of the sheet. The input tells each part what to become.
scenes.visual: Where each bundle lands, the grey sheet above takes on that bundle's tint.
scenes.narration: Different thalamic nuclei send axons to different parts of the sheet. The input tells each part what to become.

scenes.tts: Suppose you found molecular differences across the progenitors, and a map that forms without thalamic input. Which idea would that support?
scenes.visual: The left column's prediction appears without its heading: molecular differences, a map without input. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: Suppose you found molecular differences across the progenitors, and a map that forms without thalamic input. Which idea would that support?

scenes.tts: The protomap. That is what it predicts.
scenes.visual: The heading protomap fills in above that prediction.
scenes.narration: The protomap. That is what it predicts.

scenes.tts: The protocortex predicts something else. Young cortex given new input should take on features that match the input.
scenes.visual: The right column fills: new input, matching features.
scenes.narration: The protocortex predicts something else. Young cortex given new input should take on features that match the input.

scenes.tts: Both predictions came true in part.
scenes.visual: Both columns get a partial check mark.
scenes.narration: Both predictions came true in part.

scenes.tts: So the field now treats the map as drawn twice. First a sketch from the sheet, then a copy refined by its inputs.
scenes.visual: A pencil sketch of the area map, then a sharper inked version over it, with thalamic axons beneath.
scenes.narration: So the field now treats the map as drawn twice. First a sketch from the sheet, then a copy refined by its inputs.

scenes.tts: One more thing before any result: how do you read a map in a newborn mouse?
scenes.visual: A newborn mouse beside the dorsal map. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: One more thing before any result: how do you read a map in a newborn mouse?

scenes.tts: Mice lacking E M X two, and mice lacking working Pax six, die around birth, before the areas mature.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking Emx2, and mice lacking working Pax6, die around birth, before the areas mature.
scenes.visual: A mutant newborn; a timeline shows birth well before mature areas.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking Emx2, and mice lacking working Pax6, die around birth, before the areas mature.

scenes.tts: So an area in these experiments means a proxy.
scenes.visual: On screen: proxy. Three readout cards appear.
scenes.narration: So an area in these experiments means a proxy.

scenes.tts: First proxy: marker genes. A stain shows where a gene is switched on in a tissue section.
scenes.visual: A brain section with a gene stained in purple over part of the cortex. On screen: in situ hybridization.
scenes.narration: First proxy: marker genes. A stain shows where a gene is switched on in a tissue section.

scenes.tts: Some genes have borders at birth that line up with future areas.
scenes.visual: The purple stain ends at a sharp edge; a dashed line links that edge to a future area border.
scenes.narration: Some genes have borders at birth that line up with future areas.

scenes.tts: Second proxy: connections. A thalamic nucleus is a cluster of neurons. Each one projects mainly to its own part of cortex.
scenes.visual: Thalamic nuclei below, each wired mainly to its own cortical spot, with a few axons branching to neighbours.
scenes.narration: Second proxy: connections. A thalamic nucleus is a cluster of neurons. Each one projects mainly to its own part of cortex.

scenes.tts: Dye placed in one spot of cortex labels the thalamic neurons that project there, sometimes in more than one nucleus.
scenes.visual: A drop of dye on one cortical spot; colour runs back along axons, mostly into one thalamic nucleus, with a few labelled cells in a neighbour.
scenes.narration: Dye placed in one spot of cortex labels the thalamic neurons that project there, sometimes in more than one nucleus.

scenes.tts: Third proxy: the barrel field. In mice that survive past birth, a stain on flattened cortex shows the barrels as dark patches.
scenes.visual: A flattened cortex with rows of dark barrels. On screen: cytochrome oxidase stain, first postnatal week.
scenes.narration: Third proxy: the barrel field. In mice that survive past birth, a stain on flattened cortex shows the barrels as dark patches.

scenes.tts: In mice that die at birth, these proxies stand in for mature areas. Animals that survive allow later and adult measures too.
scenes.visual: The three cards stack together with a small label: early proxies; read each result at the age it was measured.
scenes.narration: In mice that die at birth, these proxies stand in for mature areas. Animals that survive allow later and adult measures too.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: the two ideas make different predictions, and early proxies are one way to test them.
scenes.visual: The prediction card beside the three proxy cards. On screen: two predictions, three proxies.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: the two ideas make different predictions, and early proxies are one way to test them.
